scope: Read-only source review, eight direct Python cryptographic/client probes and existing UNIT regressions. This review did not start, stop or restart services and does not replace the separately running deployment validation.
conclusion: No blocking correctness issue found in the reviewed change. Snapshot retention accepts an expired but authentic current credential without treating it as usable authority.
verified_boundaries: Installer-managed public key remains the trust anchor; the remote response cannot select its own trusted signer.
require_valid=False still runs _snapshot and verify_envelope: signature, exact agent, canonical shape, bound revision, all wire credential/scope fields and stored ACTIVE status remain checked.
Canonical GetAgentPassport reads the active pointer, credential and current revision under one service read lock; poisoned state fails unavailable.
ConnectedRuntime.authority() still calls PassportClient.current() with default require_valid=True; admission/commit use that path and retain local credential/scope expiry checks.
The restore report explicitly sets authorizes_execution=false and describes credential retention as diagnostics.
caveats: The diagnostic call intentionally skips VerifyPassport, including expiry and registry eligibility checks. Stored ACTIVE pointer status must not be read as currently valid permission.
An empty NOT_FOUND aggregate carries a revision asserted by the trusted local service; it contains no signed active credential.
This verifies same-host persistence across restart. It does not establish backups, disk-loss recovery, independent-host installation or authorization at a later time.
Freshness relies on the configured trusted loopback service and local host assumptions; the old signature alone is not proof of current authority.
